Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and limited range of motion.
The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the forces involved in a crash of this type, and the presenting symptoms are
plausible for a cervical strain. Over the course of 17 visits, care progressed along a typical pathway that included manual therapy,
guided home exercise, and graded activity, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms improved. Palpation and range-of-motion
testing revealed findings that support the diagnosis, while neurological screneing and several other examination components
reutrned normal results. No prior injury to the cervical region has been reported or identified in the records reviewed. Billing
review noted a duplicate charge for one service on the same date; the provider acknowledged that the second entry was a repeat
and has agreed to correct the account. Prognosis is favorable with continued self-directed exercise.
